cards.text: A former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister faces five graft charges over Sabah mineral-licence approvals. The framework at the centre of the case is a 1960 law the state voted to replace in 1999, and never switched on.
cards.sub: Shamsul Iskandar pleaded not guilty in December 2025 to charges under MACC Act section 17(a), with the alleged gratification tied to businessman Albert Tei. The modernising Mineral Enactment 1999 remains unenforced 27 years on.

cards.h: Charged December 2025, pleaded not guilty to five counts under MACC Act section 17(a)
cards.s: Section 17(a) carries up to 20 years' jail and a fine of at least five times the gratification (section 24(1)). The alleged gratification spans cash, furniture and rental payments. In April 2026 the High Court refused to move the case up from the Sessions Court, and Shamsul has filed an appeal.
cards.d: Reuters 4 Dec 2025; Bernama 8 Jan 2026; MACC Act 2009 (Act 694) ss.17(a), 24(1); Bernama 8 May 2026 (transfer rejected 28 Apr 2026, appeal filed)

cards.h: Sabah still licenses mining under a 1960 ordinance; the 1999 law meant to replace it is not in force
cards.s: Under the 1960 ordinance the Director grants prospecting licences with the Minister's approval, mining leases need Cabinet approval, and the Lands and Surveys Department issues the documents. The Mineral Enactment 1999, passed to modernise this, has sat unenforced for 27 years per the Sabah Attorney-General's Chambers.
cards.d: Sabah Mining Ordinance 1960 ss.6, 14 (SAGC official PDF); Sabah Mineral Management FAQ (issuance by Dept of Lands & Surveys); Sabah AGC Mineral Enactment 1999 page (not in force, updated May 2026)

cards.h: The alleged briber was himself charged in June 2025 over a separate RM350,000 mining-permit case
cards.s: Businessman Albert Tei was charged on 30 June 2025 alongside two Sabah assemblymen over RM350,000 in mining-permit bribes. His leaked clips in late 2024 set off the wider Sabah licensing scandal. He is now both an accused man in one case and the alleged giver in Shamsul's, an overlap that complicates the broader probe.
cards.d: The Star 30 Jun 2025; Bernama 12 Sep 2025; MalaysiaNow Nov 2025

cards.h: The cases treat the symptom; the cause is a law nobody enforced
cards.text: Every charge here treats a symptom. The cause, a 1960 licensing framework the state voted to modernise in 1999 and never brought into force, is not in any courtroom.

cards.h: A new code passed, the old one still enforced
cards.text: Picture a town that approved a new building code in 1999 but kept enforcing the 1960 one, because nobody ever signed the order to switch. The reform exists on paper; the old rules still bind.
Courts can judge the people in this case. They cannot switch on the 1999 law Sabah passed to replace the 1960 framework, and until someone does, the next licence runs on the same old rules.

sources: Reuters 4 Dec 2025; Bernama 4 Dec 2025, 8 Jan 2026, 12 Sep 2025, 8 May 2026; The Star 5 Dec 2025, 30 Jun 2025; Sabah Mining Ordinance 1960 (SAGC PDF); Sabah Mineral Enactment 1999 (SAGC, not in force); Sabah Mineral Management FAQ; MACC Act 2009 (Act 694); MalaysiaNow Nov 2025
